item.title: 'I just want to be able to sleep': Attacks in Iran rock cities and cut power
item.summary: Iranians in Tehran and Karaj tell the BBC they are exhausted and struggling to sleep after 10 days of Israeli and US attacks.

item.title: Steve Rosenberg: Russia seeks diplomatic and economic gains from Iran war
item.summary: President Putin pits himself as a potential mediator but that's not an easy sell, writes the BBC's Russia editor.

item.title: Lebanon calls for talks with Israel on plan to end Hezbollah conflict
item.summary: President Aoun outlines a path towards "permanent security and stability", as Israeli strikes targeting Hezbollah continue.

item.title: Lebanese man jailed in Germany for Hezbollah membership
item.summary: The court heard how the 35-year-old had a key role procuring products for Hezbollah's drones programme.

item.title: Five Iranian footballers granted Australian visas after anthem protest
item.summary: Concern has grown for team after one critic called them "wartime traitors" for failing to salute during the Iranian anthem.

item.title: War expands to central Beirut as Israeli strike kills Iranians in luxury hotel
item.summary: Israel's military says it targeted Quds Force operatives after a return to war with Lebanon's Hezbollah movement, but Iran says they were diplomats.

item.title: Air strikes cause black rain and 'unprecedented' pollution in Tehran, scientists say
item.summary: Air strikes have damaged at least four oil facilities since US-Israeli attacks on Iran began last month.

item.title: Mixed messages from Trump leave more questions than answers over war's end
item.summary: The US president has tried to soothe nerves over oil and markets, but his comments still lack clarity, writes Anthony Zurcher.

item.title: Acclaimed Peruvian writer Alfredo Bryce Echenique dies aged 87
item.summary: The author is best known for his novel A World for Julius, which chronicles the frivolous lives of the elite.

item.title: Signal issues scam warning to users after hackers target officials
item.summary: Signal says its systems are secure but it is taking reports of targeted attempts to hack some officials "very seriously".
